model_id: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 family; exact serving revision unverified)

correctness_confidence.basis: The four cells on page 3 sum to 118. Row and column totals give 71 and 48; the 35 exits and 12 entries explain the difference. The earlier 160+3 matches the reverse-frame total of 163 on page 2.

rigor.basis: The unrestricted strict key join precedes the documented C-prefix sensitivity. A same-name assumption does not drive the matching. The 82–113 bounds condition only on observed years. One institutional example and the absence of code collisions do not validate every additional join.

novelty.basis: The initial date used in the cited paper is taken directly from its methods. The original contribution here is the specified cross-register coverage calculation and the paired descriptive switch. Priority over all local data-quality reports is unverified.

significance.basis: A researcher using the dated project field would miss all 163 earlier map codes in the stated family and would change the recent majority by switching milestones. This matters for constructing annual series in this city. It does not adjudicate the substantive election-cycle hypothesis.

reproducibility.basis: The scripts, pinned source digests, inventories and output ledgers are retained. The public endpoints are mutable; the privileged availability of local frozen copies and the future accessibility of historical source bytes constrain reproduction elsewhere.

summary: I assessed all four rendered pages of the bound PDF and compared the core counts to both project-action ledgers and the archived citywide election table. The descriptive conclusions hold within the designated frames. I recommend this as a bounded methods working paper. I also participated in making it.
strengths: Uses the same 118 administrative actions for the milestone comparison and reports all four cells, including moves in the opposite direction.
The reverse lookup reveals an observable historical coverage failure that a match-rate calculation confined to recent projects would miss.
The source article uses effective amendment dates and the manuscript explicitly preserves this distinction. Both tables and the source notes are legible.
weaknesses: The strict 62-case subset has no separate electoral transition table in this version, so sensitivity of the majority switch to the inclusion of the 56 additional matches is unknown here.
A worked example of an added match and one of the five differing days would improve appraisal of administrative exceptions.
A citywide election flag is independently verifiable but leaves district- and parcel-level decisions unvalidated.
potential_errors: Treating these records as all zoning decisions of 2015–2024 would be wrong. The restricted code family and missing dates determine the two frames.
Assigning special-election exposure or causal intent to individual actions would require additional district and risk-set information.
A future live-data query may differ from the frozen page hashes.
strong_novelty_candidates: The joint demonstration of six missing calendar years under a plausible query and a majority reversal on the same matched recent actions may be a useful local result for administrative panel construction.
